summary.notes: REJECTED as a stronger cluster hypothesis. The only member points to EventManager::add_callback() in inc/dependencies/wp-media/event-manager/EventManager.php:25-27, which is a generic wrapper over add_filter(). The checked usage path in src/Plugin/Plugin.php:134-137 and src/Plugin/Plugin.php:289-293 shows internal bootstrap registration of SubscriberInterface instances, not a demonstrated attacker-controlled entry point or sink chain.

suggested_actions.reason: Keep separate unless a concrete subscriber trace shows that get_subscribed_events() feeds a security-relevant hook or attacker-controlled hook name into EventManager::add_callback() at inc/dependencies/wp-media/event-manager/EventManager.php:25-27.

objections.reason: The shared anchor at inc/dependencies/wp-media/event-manager/EventManager.php:26 is only a thin registration helper around add_filter(); it does not, by itself, establish a trust boundary, guard model, or sink family. The only checked in-plugin caller path is internal bootstrap code in src/Plugin/Plugin.php:134-137 and src/Plugin/Plugin.php:289-293.

open_questions.question: Do any SubscriberInterface implementations used by Plugin::load_subscribers() derive the hook name returned by get_subscribed_events() from request data or other attacker-controlled state?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without attacker influence over hook selection, EventManager::add_callback() remains a normal framework wrapper rather than an exploitable registration primitive.

open_questions.question: Does any subscriber registered through src/Plugin/Plugin.php:289-293 attach to a sensitive auth, REST, AJAX, filesystem, or option-update hook with unsafe callback behavior?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A concrete sensitive-hook trace is required before this unresolved helper can be promoted into a real security hypothesis.

missing_evidence.reason: The current pack stops at the generic registration helper and does not identify any concrete hook/callback pair.

expansion_attempts.reason: Use the single out-of-band file allowance to refute whether EventManager is exposed beyond internal plugin bootstrap.
expansion_attempts.result: Reviewed src/Plugin/Plugin.php:134-137 and src/Plugin/Plugin.php:289-293. EventManager is instantiated as an internal shared service and only used there to register container-managed SubscriberInterface instances from service providers. No attacker-controlled hook name, callback selection, or sink was established.
